::: {.explorer-intro}
This map turns collected live-chat participation into a community you can
explore. Start with a familiar chatter or stream, then follow the connections
to see where audiences overlap. Every line represents observed chat activity,
not passive viewing.
:::

```{r}
required_packages <- c("DBI", "duckdb", "dplyr", "here", "htmltools", "jsonlite", "scales")
missing_packages <- required_packages[!vapply(required_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(missing_packages) > 0L) {
  stop(
    "Install the required R packages before rendering: ",
    paste(missing_packages, collapse = ", "),
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))
source(here::here("r_scripts", "lib", "utils", "repo_env.R"))
source(here::here("r_scripts", "lib", "utils", "datalake_root.r"))
source(here::here("r_scripts", "lib", "duckdb", "db_connect.R"))
source(here::here("r_scripts", "lib", "import_data", "viewer_activity.R"))
source(here::here("r_scripts", "lib", "plots", "domains", "audience", "viewer_activity.R"))

normalize_parameter <- function(value) {
  if (is.null(value) || length(value) == 0L || is.na(value[[1]])) return(NULL)
  value <- trimws(as.character(value[[1]]))
  if (nzchar(value)) value else NULL
}

positive_integer <- function(value, default, minimum = 1L) {
  value <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(value))
  if (is.na(value) || value < minimum) default else value
}

stat_card <- function(value, label) {
  htmltools::div(
    class = "explorer-stat",
    htmltools::div(class = "explorer-stat__value", value),
    htmltools::div(class = "explorer-stat__label", label)
  )
}

talent_code <- normalize_parameter(params$talent_code)
video_id <- normalize_parameter(params$video_id)
minimum_messages <- positive_integer(params$minimum_messages, 1L)
max_videos <- positive_integer(params$max_videos, 24L)
max_users <- positive_integer(params$max_users, 100L)
network_label_count <- positive_integer(params$network_label_count, 18L)
network_height <- positive_integer(params$network_height, 760L, minimum = 420L)
overlap_max_videos <- positive_integer(params$overlap_max_videos, 16L, minimum = 2L)
network_max_selected <- positive_integer(params$network_max_selected, 40L)
overlap_max_selected <- positive_integer(params$overlap_max_selected, 30L)

load_repo_env(repo_root = here::here())
db_path <- talent_lakehouse_db_path()
if (!file.exists(db_path)) {
  stop("Unified talent lakehouse not found: ", db_path, call. = FALSE)
}
con <- duckdb_connect(db_path = db_path, read_only = TRUE)

viewer_video_activity <- load_viewer_video_activity(con, talent_code) %>%
  filter(.data$message_count >= minimum_messages)
if (nrow(viewer_video_activity) == 0L) {
  stop("No collected chat activity matched the selected scope.", call. = FALSE)
}
video_explorer_data <- viewer_activity_video_explorer_prep(viewer_video_activity)

engagement_network <- viewer_activity_bipartite_prep(
  viewer_video_activity,
  video_id = video_id,
  max_videos = max_videos,
  max_users = max_users
)
if (nrow(engagement_network$engagement_edges) == 0L) {
  stop("No network edges matched the selected video and message threshold.", call. = FALSE)
}
community_shape <- viewer_activity_community_shape_prep(
  viewer_video_activity,
  max_overlap_videos = overlap_max_videos
)

scope_parts <- c(
  if (is.null(talent_code)) "all talents" else paste("talent", talent_code),
  if (!is.null(video_id)) paste("video", video_id),
  paste("at least", minimum_messages, "message(s) per chatter–video relationship")
)

htmltools::div(
  class = "explorer-stats",
  stat_card(scales::comma(nrow(community_shape$profiles)), "Community chatters"),
  stat_card(
    scales::comma(dplyr::n_distinct(viewer_video_activity$video_id)),
    "Streams in scope"
  ),
  stat_card(scales::comma(nrow(engagement_network$users)), "Chatters in opening map"),
  stat_card(
    scales::comma(sum(viewer_video_activity$message_count)),
    "Community messages"
  )
)
```

```{r}
htmltools::p(
  class = "explorer-scope",
  paste("Current scope:", paste(scope_parts, collapse = " · "))
)
```

```{r}
viewer_activity_video_explorer_d3(
  video_explorer_data,
  view = "network",
  initial_video_count = max_videos,
  initial_video_ids = video_id,
  max_selected = network_max_selected,
  max_users = max_users,
  label_count = network_label_count,
  height = network_height
)
```

## How to interpret this map

- **Blue nodes are chatters.** A connection means the person posted at least
  one collected chat message in that stream.
- **Gold nodes are streams.** Shared chatters reveal audience overlap between
  streams.
- **Purple nodes are creators.** Gray links identify which creator hosted
  each stream; they are context links rather than audience activity.

The display is intentionally bounded to the most active selected streams and
chatters so the network remains usable. It does not imply that people outside
the display were absent. “First observed” and related measures describe the
collected chat record, not a person’s first-ever interaction with a creator.
The Videos menu searches every stream in the current talent and message scope.
`max_videos` controls only the initial selection, not which titles are
available. To keep the force layout readable, `network_max_selected` limits how
many videos can be drawn simultaneously.

## The shape of the full community

The opening network is useful for following individual relationships, but a
node-link view becomes crowded before it can show the whole community. The
next views use every chatter in the selected scope rather than only the
chatters displayed in the opening map.

### Community layers

This view separates occasional participation from repeat and core engagement.
Bar length is the number of chatters; the annotation shows how much of the
community’s conversation each layer produced.

- **Drop-in:** chatted in one stream.
- **Returning:** chatted in two or three streams.
- **Regular:** chatted in four to seven streams.
- **Core:** chatted in eight or more streams.

```{r}
viewer_activity_community_shape_d3(community_shape, view = "segments")
```

### Engagement landscape

Each square contains the number of chatters with that combination of stream
breadth and message intensity. This distinguishes, for example, prolific
single-stream visitors from people who participate consistently across the
creator’s catalog.

```{r}
viewer_activity_community_shape_d3(community_shape, view = "landscape")
```

### Stream audience overlap

This is the adjacency-matrix form of a stream-to-stream network. Darker purple
means the two streams share a larger proportion of their combined chatter
audience, measured with Jaccard similarity. Hover for the shared-chatter count
and exact similarity. Use the Compare menu to choose any videos in the current
scope; the matrix is recalculated immediately for that exact subset. The
diagonal is gray because it compares each stream with itself.
`overlap_max_videos` controls the initial comparison and
`overlap_max_selected` keeps a selected matrix readable.

```{r}
viewer_activity_video_explorer_d3(
  video_explorer_data,
  view = "overlap",
  initial_video_count = overlap_max_videos,
  initial_video_ids = video_id,
  max_selected = overlap_max_selected
)
```
